check: Treatment and outcome are clearly defined
why_it_matters: A policy acts on a specific intervention and optimizes a specific response.

check: Treatment cost is included or explicitly justified
why_it_matters: Positive gross effects can become negative net effects after cost.
Policy rules must be available before deciding treatment.
Unsupported regions make action recommendations extrapolative.
Targeting depends on ranking more than average effect alone.

check: Policy value is compared with simple baselines
why_it_matters: A learned policy should beat treat-none, treat-all, random, and simple top-k rules.

check: Treatment rate and budget are reported
why_it_matters: Policy value depends on how many units are treated.
Overall gain can hide uneven treatment allocation.

check: Uncertainty or conservative margins are considered
why_it_matters: Policies based on noisy effects can over-treat borderline units.
Offline policy value from observational data is not enough by itself.
